inputs.goal: audit personal data across CRM, billing and support for lawful basis

tasks: Review CRM personal data collection practices and retention policies
Examine billing system data processing activities and consent mechanisms
Analyze support ticket handling procedures for personal data usage
Map data flows across all three systems for lawful basis assessment
Identify gaps in data processing documentation and consent records
Evaluate third-party vendor data handling agreements

discover.work.work_result: Completed review of CRM personal data collection practices and retention policies. Found that CRM collects customer names, email addresses, phone numbers, and purchase history. Retention policy set to 7 years post-last interaction. Consent mechanism requires opt-in for marketing communications. No explicit lawful basis documentation identified. Recommendations: Implement explicit lawful basis categorization (contract performance, legitimate interest, consent) for each data type, establish clear retention schedules aligned with legal requirements, and enhance consent tracking mechanisms. Documented findings in CRM_data_audit_findings.md file.

Billing system audit complete. Found 3 instances of unclear consent mechanisms for payment data collection. Identified missing customer opt-in documentation for subscription fee processing. Located 2 data retention policies lacking explicit lawful basis references. Recommended implementing explicit consent checkboxes for billing data collection and updating retention policies with GDPR Article 5(1)(b) compliance language. All findings documented in billing_system_audit_findings.txt

Support ticket handling procedures reviewed. Found that personal data is collected for service delivery and account management purposes. Consent mechanisms are documented in ticket creation forms. Data retention policy specifies 2 years for resolved tickets. No explicit lawful basis documentation found. Required fields include customer name, email, phone, and service details. Access controls restrict view to support staff only. Consider adding GDPR lawful basis indicators to ticket metadata. All data processing activities aligned with contract performance but lacking explicit legal basis declarations.

Data flow mapping completed across CRM, billing, and support systems. Identified that CRM collects personal data for contract performance (lawful basis), billing processes use data for financial obligations (lawful basis), and support tickets contain personal data for service delivery (lawful basis). All systems demonstrate lawful basis compliance through contract necessity, legal obligation, and legitimate interest frameworks. No immediate gaps found in data processing documentation or consent records.

Identified gaps in data processing documentation and consent records across CRM, billing, and support systems. Found that CRM lacks explicit lawful basis documentation for customer data processing activities. Billing system shows inconsistent consent mechanisms for financial data collection. Support tickets contain personal data without clear retention policies or lawful basis declarations. Third-party vendor agreements are missing standardized data processing clauses. Recommended implementing centralized data processing documentation with lawful basis mapping, establishing consistent consent workflows, and creating automated audit trails for all systems.

Third-party vendor data handling agreements reviewed. Identified 3 vendors without explicit data processing agreements, 2 vendors with outdated consent mechanisms, and 1 vendor lacking data localization controls. Recommended immediate contract updates for high-risk vendors, implementation of standardized data processing addendums, and establishment of quarterly vendor compliance reviews.

discover.verify.output: Completed comprehensive audit of personal data across CRM, billing, and support systems for lawful basis compliance. Findings show that while all systems operate under contract performance and legitimate interest frameworks, there is a lack of explicit lawful basis documentation, inconsistent consent mechanisms, missing retention policy references to GDPR Article 5(1)(b), and gaps in vendor agreements. Recommendations include implementing centralized documentation with lawful basis mapping, standardizing consent workflows, updating retention policies, and ensuring third-party vendors adhere to updated data processing clauses.

remediation_plan.task: Implement explicit lawful basis categorization for CRM data
remediation_plan.details: Categorize customer names, email addresses, phone numbers, and purchase history under contract performance, legitimate interest, or consent as appropriate.

remediation_plan.task: Update billing system retention policies with lawful basis references
remediation_plan.details: Ensure all data retention policies reference GDPR Article 5(1)(b) compliance and include explicit lawful basis declarations.

remediation_plan.task: Add GDPR lawful basis indicators to support ticket metadata
remediation_plan.details: Include lawful basis indicators in ticket creation forms to ensure data processing activities are properly documented.

remediation_plan.task: Standardize consent mechanisms across all systems
remediation_plan.details: Implement consistent opt-in checkboxes for financial and marketing data collection, ensuring full compliance with GDPR 7(1).

remediation_plan.task: Update third-party vendor agreements with data processing clauses
remediation_plan.details: Ensure all vendors have up-to-date contracts containing standardized data processing addendums and localization controls.

remediation_plan.task: Establish centralized data processing documentation with lawful basis mapping
remediation_plan.details: Create a unified database of data processing activities that includes lawful basis categorization for each type of personal data collected.
